resources.string:
Screens notifications from the apps chosen with the icon picker on the right.

Number Rules and Text Rules with Title / Body enabled under Apply to Notifications are checked against the notification, the same way as a real incoming SMS.
If the result is Block, the notification is dismissed.

Phone numbers in the notification\'s Title / Body are also checked by the Basic Rules Contacts (when blocking non-contacts) and Database, if Title / Body is on in their settings, without needing a Number Rule.

This works independently of the SMS switch above, and requires Notification Access permission.

Some apps\' notifications may not be dismissed quickly enough to avoid a brief alert (sound/vibration) from the original app before SpamBlocker Extended can act.
If this is annoying, you can disable that app\'s own notifications in system settings, then use Alerts instead to be notified only for explicitly allowed notifications.

/ Body
Check this rule against notifications from the apps chosen in Notifications (in Screening).

The regex is searched for anywhere within the notification\'s title/body, it doesn\'t need to match the whole text.
Logs are saved only for workflows with the <highlight>Schedule</highlight> trigger type.

Enable auto-reporting exclusively for specific regex rules by matching against their rule descriptions.

Example:
  Rule 1: .*won.*claim.*
  Description: scam
  Rule 2: .*balance.*bank.*
  Description: reminder

  Setting this filter to scam ensures only calls blocked by rule 1 get auto-reported.

The default setting .* enables auto-reporting for calls blocked by any regex rule.

Tip:
This is a regex field, match multiple rules using a pattern like (scam|ads|political).

Turn on Screening > Calls and allow SpamBlocker Extended as the call screening app.

<b>On each incoming call</b>
1. Rules are checked by priority: Basic Rules (Contacts, Database, STIR, Repeated Call…), then Number Rules on the number and Text Rules on the caller name.
2. The first rule that matches decides.
3. No match: the call rings as usual.

<b>When blocked</b>
The call is handled by the Block Type: Reject, Silence or Hang Up.
It is logged in the Call tab, so you can review it and create a rule from it.

<b>Tip</b>
Use Test in Settings to see which rule a number would hit.

Turn on Screening > SMS/MMS. SpamBlocker Extended does not need to be the default SMS app.

<b>On each incoming SMS</b>
1. Number Rules check the sender and Text Rules check the message, together with Basic Rules (Contacts, Database…), by priority.
2. Allowed: SpamBlocker Extended shows the notification.
3. Blocked: no notification, or a silent one, as set in the rule.

Note
- The message still stays in your SMS app, it is only filtered, not deleted.
- Turn off your SMS app\'s notifications to avoid getting them twice.
- MMS (also group messages) are checked by text only.
- RCS / chat messages are not SMS: screen them with Notifications instead.

Turn on Screening > Notifications, grant Notification Access, and pick the apps with the icon next to the switch.

<b>On each notification from those apps</b>
1. Number and Text Rules with Title / Body on are checked against it.
2. Phone numbers found in the Title / Body are checked by Contacts and Database, per their Title / Body settings.
3. The first match by priority decides. A contact in the Title (allow, 10) beats a spam number in the Body (block, 0).
4. Blocked: the notification is dismissed. The message itself stays in the app.

<b>Voicemail</b>
Voicemail Notification takes the caller\'s number out of a voicemail app\'s notification and checks it like a call.

<b>Tip</b>
To hear only wanted notifications, turn off the app\'s own sound and use Alerts for allowed ones.
